easy.explanation: Jeremiah 6:1 says that evil appears out of the north.
easy.q: From which direction does evil appear?

easy.explanation: They were told to gather themselves to flee out of Jerusalem.
easy.q: What were the children of Benjamin told to do?

easy.explanation: The shepherds with their flocks would pitch their tents against her round about.
easy.q: What did the shepherds pitch around Jerusalem?

medium.explanation: The trumpet and fire sign served as warnings because evil was coming from the north.
medium.q: Why were the trumpet and fire sign used?

answers: The enemy intended to act quickly
medium.explanation: The enemies said, “Let us go by night, and let us destroy her palaces.”
medium.q: What does the command to attack at night show?

medium.explanation: The fire sign was a signal that could warn people of the approaching danger.
medium.q: What does “set up a sign of fire” most likely mean in context?

challenge.explanation: The people are warned, the enemy surrounds the city, and plans are made to attack.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the danger in these verses?

challenge.explanation: The phrase expresses urgency as daylight ends and danger approaches.
challenge.q: What does “the day goeth away” suggest?

answers: As a city threatened and surrounded
challenge.explanation: Jerusalem is surrounded by enemies who prepare war against her.
challenge.q: How is Jerusalem portrayed in this passage?

paragraphs.title: Jerusalem Punished for Oppression and Evil

easy.explanation: The city was described as wholly oppression in the midst of her.
easy.q: What was found in the midst of Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “Be thou instructed, O Jerusalem.”
easy.q: Who was told to be instructed?

easy.explanation: The remnant would be thoroughly gleaned as a vine by a grapegatherer.
easy.q: What was the remnant of Israel compared to?

answers: Because Jerusalem was filled with oppression
Because the people wanted to leave
medium.explanation: The LORD commands the siege against a city full of oppression.
medium.q: Why is the siege presented as a command from the LORD?

answers: Its violence leads to visitation and destruction
medium.explanation: The city’s violence and spoil are presented as the reason for the coming judgment.
medium.q: What is the relationship between Jerusalem’s evil and the judgment described?

medium.explanation: A remnant is the part that remains after others have been removed.
medium.q: What does “the remnant of Israel” mean here?

answers: That wickedness continually flows from Jerusalem
That the city is free from sin
challenge.explanation: As a fountain casts out water, Jerusalem continually casts out wickedness.
challenge.q: What does the fountain image emphasize?

answers: The violence is repeated and ongoing
The city hears only peaceful words
challenge.explanation: “Continually” shows that grief, wounds, violence, and spoil are persistent.
challenge.q: What does “continually” emphasize in the phrase about violence and spoil?

answers: They will be gathered carefully and completely
They will be left entirely alone
challenge.explanation: The grapegatherer returns to the vine to collect what remains.
challenge.q: What does the image of gleaning teach about the remnant?

paragraphs.title: A People Who Refuse to Listen

easy.explanation: Their ear is called uncircumcised, and they cannot hearken.
easy.q: How are the people’s ears described?

easy.explanation: The verse says the word of the LORD was unto them a reproach.
easy.q: What was the word of the LORD to them?

easy.explanation: They said, “Peace, peace; when there is no peace.”
easy.q: What did the false healers say?

answers: The people do not know the city
medium.explanation: From the least to the greatest, and from prophet to priest, all deal falsely.
medium.q: Why is judgment directed at every level of society?

answers: It was spoken only to foreign nations
medium.explanation: The verse immediately says that there was no peace.
medium.q: What was wrong with the promise of “Peace, peace”?

answers: Something viewed with shame or contempt
medium.explanation: The people treated the word of the LORD with contempt rather than delight.
medium.q: What does “reproach” mean in this context?

answers: Both prevent people from facing the true evil
challenge.explanation: The people reject the LORD’s warning and accept deceptive claims of peace.
challenge.q: What connection exists between deaf ears and false assurances of peace?

answers: Corruption reaches every social and religious level
challenge.explanation: The accusation extends from the least to the greatest and from prophet to priest.
challenge.q: What does the inclusion of both prophets and priests show?

answers: They willingly reject the word of the LORD
challenge.explanation: The statement shows deliberate rejection, not merely an inability to hear.
challenge.q: What does “they have no delight in it” reveal?

paragraphs.title: Rejecting the Good Way and Bringing Disaster

easy.explanation: They were told to ask for the old paths and find the good way.
easy.q: What were the people told to seek in the ways?

answers: Listen for the sound of the trumpet
easy.explanation: The watchmen were told to hearken to the sound of the trumpet.
easy.q: What were the watchmen told to do?

easy.explanation: The people did not hearken to God’s words or law, but rejected it.
easy.q: What did the people do to the law?

answers: It results from their thoughts and actions
It comes without relation to their conduct
medium.explanation: The disaster is presented as the result of their thoughts and refusal to obey.
medium.q: Why is the coming evil called the fruit of their thoughts?

answers: The watchmen warn, but the people refuse to listen
The watchmen remain silent, and the people obey
The watchmen promise peace, and the people celebrate
medium.explanation: The watchmen call them to hear the trumpet, but they answer, “We will not hearken.”
medium.q: What is the relationship between the watchmen and the people?

medium.explanation: Walking in the good way would bring rest and peace to their souls.
medium.q: What does “rest for your souls” mean?

answers: It is connected to the people’s moral choices
challenge.explanation: Their refusal of the good way, warnings, and law leads to the described disaster.
challenge.q: What does rejection of the good way reveal about the source of disaster?

answers: Their conduct was evil and disobedient
They did not know how to offer them
challenge.explanation: Offerings cannot make disobedient conduct acceptable before the LORD.
challenge.q: Why were the incense and sacrifices unacceptable?

answers: It points to the proven good way that they should follow
It describes a newly invented road
It identifies a road leading only to the enemy
challenge.explanation: The old paths represent the good way in which the people were urged to walk.
challenge.q: How does “the old paths” support the message of the passage?

paragraphs.title: The Northern People and the Fear They Inspire

easy.explanation: The passage says that a people comes from the north country.
easy.q: From where does the great people come?

easy.explanation: They lay hold on bow and spear.
easy.q: What weapons do the enemies carry?

easy.explanation: She was told to gird herself with sackcloth.
easy.q: What was the daughter of the people told to wear?

answers: They are cruel and have no mercy
medium.explanation: The enemy is described as cruel and without mercy.
medium.q: Why are the approaching people feared?

answers: Do not go forth or walk there
medium.explanation: The people were told not to go into the field or walk by the way because of the enemy’s sword and fear.
medium.q: What instruction was given about the field and the way?

medium.explanation: Fear surrounds them because of the approaching enemy and sword.
medium.q: What does “fear is on every side” mean?

answers: The destruction is expected to be sudden and near
The people are secure from attack
challenge.explanation: They are told to mourn in advance because the spoiler will suddenly come.
challenge.q: What does the call to mourn before the spoiler arrives suggest?

answers: As a great, cruel, well-armed army
As a small group without weapons
challenge.explanation: The enemy is great, cruel, armed with bows and spears, and arranged for war.
challenge.q: How is the enemy described beyond its northern origin?

answers: Fear has weakened their strength and courage
challenge.explanation: Their weakened hands express terror, anguish, and helplessness.
challenge.q: What does “our hands wax feeble” reveal?

paragraphs.title: Testing the People and Rejected Silver

answers: To test and examine their way
easy.explanation: He was appointed as a tower and fortress so he could know and try their way.
easy.q: Why was the prophet set among the people?

easy.explanation: They are called grievous revolters who walk with slanders.
The final verse says they shall be called reprobate silver.
easy.q: What are the people called at the end?

medium.explanation: They are described as revolters, slanderers, and corrupters.
medium.q: What did examining their way reveal?

answers: The purification process fails to remove the evil
The metal has no connection to the people
medium.explanation: The founder melts in vain because the wicked are not plucked away.
medium.q: What does the refiner’s image teach?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes something tested and rejected as unacceptable.

answers: Both examine what is genuine and what is corrupt
challenge.explanation: The prophet tests the people’s way, while the refiner tests and purifies metal.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the prophet’s task and the refiner’s work?

answers: Even attempted purification has not removed the evil
There was no fire at all
challenge.explanation: The refining effort is vain because the wicked are not separated from the metal.
challenge.q: What does the burned bellows and consumed lead show?

answers: Their rebellion and corruption show that they are rejected
challenge.explanation: Their slander, rebellion, and corruption make them unfit, like silver rejected by the refiner.
challenge.q: How does the people’s description support the name “reprobate silver”?
